Tests of the standardized ratios of a Cox fit

Source: R/test_cox.R
test.cox.Rd

Tests every provider's indirect standardized ratio \(O_j / E_j\) (see standardize.cox()) against 1, treating the observed count \(O_j\) as Poisson with mean \(E_j\), and flags the providers with more or fewer events than expected. These are the tests of the survival measures (SMR, SHR, STrR, SWR).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cox'
test(
  fit,
  statistic = c("midp", "exact", "wald"),
  dispersion = c("none", "deviance"),
  providers = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  min_expected = 0,
  null_model = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted by fit_cox().

statistic

"midp" (default; the two-sided mid-p Poisson test turned into a z statistic, the SMR convention), "exact" (the two-sided Poisson test with exact or Byar limits, the SWR convention; theoretical null only) or "wald" (\(\log(O_j / E_j)\) over its standard error \(\sqrt{\phi / O_j}\), the SHR convention).

dispersion

for statistic = "wald": "none" (default; \(\phi = 1\)) or "deviance" (\(\phi\) = the Poisson deviance of the patient-level counts about \((O_j / E_j) e_k\) over its degrees of freedom, as PROC GENMOD's DSCALE; the units are the patients when pp_data() has a patient column, the rows otherwise).

providers

optional subset of provider identifiers to report.

level

confidence level; the significance level is 1 - level.

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

min_expected

providers with fewer than min_expected expected events are dropped from the result (the measures use 3, so that an empirical null fitted on the result does not see them). Default 0.

null_model

optional null model: a pp_null object or a function of the result returning one, for instance function(t) null_model("empirical", t, size = t$person_time, grouping = "quantile") (the survival measures group providers by quartiles of person-time); the result is then passed through calibrate(). Not available for the exact test.

...

unused.

Value

A data frame of class pp_test with one row per tested provider: provider, estimate (the ratio \(O_j / E_j\)), se (Wald only; the standard error of the log ratio), null_value (1), statistic, p, flag (1 more events than expected, -1 fewer, 0 not different, NA not testable), lower, upper (limits for the ratio), observed, expected, person_time. Attributes test (the settings, including phi) and sizes.

Details

The mid-p statistic is \(z = \pm\Phi^{-1}(p)\) with \(p = \max(10^{-6}, \min(P_{low}, P_{high}) / 2)\), \(P_{low} = 2 F(O_j) - f(O_j)\), \(P_{high} = 2 [1 - F(O_j - 1)] - f(O_j)\), \(F\) and \(f\) the Poisson distribution and mass functions with mean \(E_j\), the sign negative when the lower tail is the smaller. Its confidence limits invert the (calibrated) test: the Poisson means at which the provider's count is just significant, divided by \(E_j\), so that a limit excludes 1 exactly when the provider is flagged.

The exact test's p-value is \(2 P(X \ge O_j)\) for a ratio above 1 and \(2 P(X \le O_j)\) otherwise, capped at 0.999; its limits are the exact chi-square limits when \(E_j < 100\) and Byar's approximation otherwise.

The Wald limits are \(\exp[\log(O_j / E_j) \pm c\, se]\); a provider with no events has no Wald statistic.

References

He K, Schaubel DE (2015). Standardized mortality ratio for evaluating center-specific mortality: assessment and alternative. Statistics in Biosciences, 7, 296-321.

Breslow NE, Day NE (1987). Statistical Methods in Cancer Research, Volume II: The Design and Analysis of Cohort Studies. IARC.

Examples

s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 30, type = "survival", seed = 1)
ps <- pp_data(s, x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", time = "stop", start = "start",
              event = "event", cutoff = 0, message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_cox(ps)
test(fit)
#> Provider tests: midp statistic, poisson variance; null ratio = 1; two.sided, level 0.95
#>   30 providers: 3 above, 4 below, 23 not different, 0 not tested
#>  provider estimate se null_value statistic        p flag  lower upper observed

#>      P002   1.2270 NA          1    1.0568 0.290581    0 0.8251 1.761       27
#>      P003   1.1627 NA          1    0.4457 0.655800    0 0.5085 2.300        7
#>      P004   0.7691 NA          1   -1.0881 0.276549    0 0.4630 1.206       17
#>      P005   1.4076 NA          1    1.4777 0.139493    0 0.8840 2.135       20
#>      P006   1.4212 NA          1    1.8140 0.069676    0 0.9699 2.015       29
#>  expected person_time
#>     3.519       6.915
#>    22.005      48.263
#>     6.020      13.663
#>    22.104      45.257
#>    14.209      31.364
#>    20.405      45.432
#>   ... 24 more rows
test(fit, statistic = "wald", dispersion = "deviance")
#> Provider tests: wald statistic, poisson variance; null ratio = 1; two.sided, level 0.95
#>   30 providers: 2 above, 3 below, 25 not different, 0 not tested
